description.content:
Exchanges an email and password for a bearer token. The response also
carries the token's expiry and the caller's role and tenant, so a
client never needs to decode the token.

A wrong password and an unknown email get the same
`invalid_credentials`. The email is matched ignoring case. The body
may be at most 64 KiB.

Each client address may make 10 attempts a minute, right or wrong,
and all 10 at once after a quiet minute. An IPv6 address shares its
allowance with the rest of its /64. Only attempts that reach the
password check count, and their responses carry the `RateLimit-*`
headers.

item.name: Ingest
item.description:
Getting events in. Three paths, one normalizer: a single JSON event, an
NDJSON batch from the collector, and a whole vendor export file.

description.content:
Accepts one vendor event as JSON, normalizes it, and stores it. The
event is committed before this call returns, so it is searchable
immediately.

A body that is not a JSON object is answered with 400 `invalid_json`.
An event that is JSON but cannot be stored is answered with 200, and
`errors[0]` says why, as it would for a line of a batch. The body may
be at most 1 MiB.

Caddy exposes this as `POST /ingest` at the edge, which is the form
the sample senders use.

Ingest takes the ingest key or an admin's token, and both may write to
any tenant, so the event names its own. A viewer's token is refused
with 403 `permission_denied`.

event reports why in `errors[0]`.

item.name: Ingest a batch of events as NDJSON

request.name: Ingest a batch of events as NDJSON

description.content:
One JSON event per line. This is what the collector forwards after
buffering syslog and file input, sending the ingest key.

A malformed or unmappable line does not fail the request: the response
reports `accepted` and `rejected` counts with per-line detail. This is
deliberate. The collector retries a 5xx, 408 or 429 from its disk
buffer until it succeeds, and drops the whole batch on any other
status. Failing a batch for one poison line would either stall the
buffer behind it forever or throw away every good record with it. A
non-2xx status here means the request was unusable as a whole, not that
some records were bad.

The collector does not read the response, so the server also logs
each request that had rejected records, with counts by code.

Blank lines are skipped and are not records. A line may be at most
1 MiB, and the body at most 32 MiB.

response.name: Batch processed; counts report how many records stored.

description.content:
Same wire format and same per-record error handling as the batch
endpoint, for uploading a vendor export directly:

```
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
     --data-binary @samples/json/aws_cloudtrail.ndjson \
     https://localhost/api/v1/ingest/file
```

`tenant` and `source` may be supplied as query parameters, and apply
only to records that do not carry their own.

The example needs `-H "Authorization: Bearer $INGEST_TOKEN"` once
`INGEST_TOKEN` is exported from `.env`, or an admin's token.

Filtered, time-ordered list of normalized events.

Results are paged with an opaque cursor rather than an offset. Events
arrive continuously, so an offset would shift under the reader between
pages, showing duplicates and silently skipping rows. Pass the
`next_cursor` from one response as `cursor` on the next request; its
absence means there are no more results.

A cursor is tied to the filters it was produced with. Re-using one with
different filters is rejected with `invalid_cursor` rather than
silently paging through a different result set. `from` and `to` may be
left out after the first page; the cursor remembers the window.

Any other unusable parameter is rejected with `invalid_parameter`. A
search still running after 10 seconds, usually a free-text one over a
wide window, is cancelled with 503 `search_timeout`.

Omitting it is always safe and is the common case — it returns
everything the caller may see.

about two and a half minutes after the event that completes it.

variable.description: Who Sign in signs in as. An admin may ingest and search; a viewer, such as viewer@demoa.local, may only search.
The password for email: ADMIN_PASSWORD or VIEWER_PASSWORD in .env.
Sent by every request that needs a credential. Sign in sets it. For the ingest requests, the ingest key (INGEST_TOKEN in .env) works too.

description.content:
Multi-tenant log management: ingest events from many sources, normalize them
into one schema, search and count them, and raise alerts when they repeat.

## Shape of this API

Ingest is permissive and search is strict. A sender may post whatever its
vendor emits; unknown fields are preserved verbatim in `raw` and stay
searchable. What comes back out of search is the normalized schema, with
every field named as in the common event schema.

## Errors

Every error is the same JSON envelope: a stable `code` to match on, a
human `message` that may change, and `request_id` correlating with the
server log. `422` additionally carries per-field failures in `errors[]`;
no other status does.

A `404` or `405` from an unrouted path is generated by the Go HTTP mux and
is plain text rather than this envelope.

## Authentication

People sign in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and send the token it
returns as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A token lasts 12 hours and
cannot be refreshed; sign in again when it expires.

Senders that aren't people, such as the collector and the sample scripts,
use the ingest key instead: `INGEST_TOKEN` from the appliance's `.env`,
sent the same way. It may send events for any tenant and do nothing else.

There are two roles. An `admin` reads every tenant, may ingest for any of
them, and creates alert rules. A `viewer` belongs to one tenant, reads only
that tenant, and may not ingest or create alert rules. Each endpoint lists
the credentials it accepts.

A request is refused in one of two ways:

- `401` when it didn't prove who is calling: `authentication_required`
  when no credential was sent, `invalid_token` when the one sent is
  malformed, expired or not recognised. A client holding a token should
  discard it and sign in again.
- `403` when the caller is known but may not do this:
  `permission_denied`, or `tenant_not_permitted` when the request names a
  tenant outside the caller's reach.
